headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: EBAY, SNDK, META, IONQ, LITE Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Memory stocks – Shares of memory chip companies slid after China's CXMT said it will begin producing next-generation memory chips that will compete for market share with U.S. and Korean companies. Micron Technology lost about 3%, as did Seagate Technology . Western Digital fell more than 2% and Sandisk lost more than 5%. The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) shed 4%. eBay — The e-commerce company jumped more than 5% after Morgan Stanley dubbed eBay a top pick and lifted its price target to $132, suggesting nearly 18% upside. The firm estimates that the $27 billion live selling market – which involves selling products in real time through a livestream – is "driving 40%+ of EBAY's growth." Meta Platforms — Shares gained more than 3% on speculation that Meta is gearing up to roll out a new artificial intelligence model codenamed Watermelon, according to StreetAccount. On Monday, Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang posted on social media platform X "vibes kinda good," followed by a watermelon emoji. Optical stocks — Investors took a few chips off the table after artificial intelligence plays saw a rebound last Friday. Ciena was last down more than 8%, while Lumentum slid 9%. Applied Optoelectronics fell 6%. Salesforce — The stock rose almost 2% after a Bank of America double upgrade to buy from underperform. The bank argued that artificial intelligence should not disrupt, rather "deepen dependence" on the software name. First Solar — Shares gained 2% after Truist upgraded the solar name to buy from hold. The bank is confident in the growth and strong demand in the solar market over the coming years, as well as First Solar's pricing power in the industry. Biogen — Shares of Biogen rose nearly 4% after analysts at JPMorgan upgraded the biotech name to overweight from neutral . The firm cited several clinical readouts in 2027 as catalysts for Biogen. SLM — Shares advanced 4% after the company, which deals with the administration of education loans, was upgraded by Morgan Stanley to overweight from equal weight. The stock down 15% year to date is a buying opportunity, Morgan Stanley said, given its favorable valuation. Mattel — The toymaker rose 1% after analysts at Seaport upgraded the stock to buy from neutral. With speculation of a potential takeover swirling, "we think investors are taking a closer look at toy stocks and realizing that there's underappreciated value," the research firm wrote. IonQ — Shares fell more than 8% after the company bought cybersecurity firm Elisity for $1.3 billion . Quantum computing stocks Rigetti Computing and D-Wave Quantum each shed roughly 5% in sympathy. — CNBC's Nick Wells and Tom Rotunno contributed reporting.

headlines.summary: McDonald's is targeting growth in chicken and beverages, but Consumer Edge data shows Chick-fil-A and coffee chains gaining in customer spending.
headlines.article_text: McDonald's chicken and beverage growth faces rivals Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points McDonald's is pegging its growth hopes on chicken and beverages, but data shows it is losing spending share to key rivals like Chick-fil-A. Coffee chains like Dutch Bros. and Starbucks are also gaining ground, according to Consumer Edge. McDonald's growth plan includes rolling out hand-breaded chicken items and bringing grilled chicken back to its menu. In this article MCD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A chicken sandwich from McDonald's is shown in Chicago, Illinois, May 6, 2021. Scott Olson | Getty Images McDonald's is betting on chicken and beverages to fuel its next phase of growth, but new consumer spending data suggests the fast-food giant faces stiff competition from rivals that specialize in those areas. At its September investor day, McDonald's outlined plans to gain an additional 1.5 percentage points of global market share in both chicken and beverages by 2030. The chain identified the categories as significant opportunities to expand its business beyond beef. CEO Chris Kempczinski told CNBC the size of those markets underscores the potential upside. "Chicken is a $130 billion category. We have about a 20% share of chicken. Beverages is about a $230 billion category. We have a 10% share of beverages," Kempczinski said, saying McDonald's has more room to grow in those areas than in the $50 billion global beef category, where it has about a 40% share. But new data indicates McDonald's could have a tough task in gaining spending from chicken and drink rivals. Many of the restaurant chains winning the most spending from McDonald's diners specialize in those two segments, according to exclusive data shared by Consumer Edge, which tracks credit and debit card transactions. Among McDonald's customers, Chick-fil-A gained 0.58 percentage points of limited-service restaurant spending in the third quarter compared with a year earlier, making it the biggest gainer among the chains tracked by Consumer Edge. Coffee businesses are also capturing more spending from McDonald's customers. Drive-thru-only chain 7 Brew added 0.4 percentage points, while Starbucks , Dutch Bros. Coffee and Dunkin' also ranked among the top 10 gainers. Together, the four coffee chains added 0.88 percentage points of spending share. McDonald's remained by far the largest individual chain in customers' overall limited-service restaurant spending, but its share declined from a year earlier. Restaurant Brands International -owned Burger King, meanwhile, gained 0.24 percentage points, the largest increase among burger chains. "There’s a big battle for a smaller amount of restaurant spend as people become more selective in what they spend," said Michael Gunther, Consumer Edge senior vice president. The data says only so much about the competitive landscape for McDonald's in the chicken and drink spaces, in part because they don't track exactly what customers are ordering at the counter. "If they [McDonald's] are able to attract diners with interesting options, it could work,” Gunther added. While McDonald's has struggled with sluggish sales, executives have said they saw signs of improvement toward the end of the third quarter. At its investor day, McDonald's said U.S. comparable sales were slightly negative in July and August, but the company said it expected September to turn positive. Consumer Edge data similarly showed McDonald's year-over-year spending share declines narrowing across every income group in September. Wall Street has also questioned how quickly the chicken and beverage strategy can deliver. Bernstein analyst Danilo Gargiulo said after McDonald's investor day that U.S. beverage launches had not generated enough sales to offset broader weakness, while the company's next chicken platform — which includes hand-breaded chicken and grilled chicken menu items — was further away than he expected. "The scale of investment required to deliver [the company's growth plan] McDonald's Next was above our expectations and introduces additional pressure on near-term earnings," said Gargiulo in his note. He has a market perform rating on the stock and $295 price target. Shares closed around $235 on Friday.
